# ============================================================
# VALIDAÇÃO E COBERTURA TEMPORAL DA BASE
# ============================================================

print("Tipo da coluna:", df_online["data_publicacao"].dtype)
print("Datas inválidas ou ausentes:", df_online["data_publicacao"].isna().sum())
print("Data mais antiga:", df_online["data_publicacao"].min())
print("Data mais recente:", df_online["data_publicacao"].max())

print("\nQuantidade de notícias por ano:")
quantidade_por_ano = (
    df_online.dropna(subset=["data_publicacao"])
      .groupby(df_online["data_publicacao"].dt.year)
      .size()
      .sort_index()
)
print(quantidade_por_ano)

# Exibe exemplos de datas que não puderam ser convertidas, caso existam.
datas_invalidas = df_online.loc[
    df_online["data_publicacao"].isna(),
    ["id", "classe", "data_publicacao_original"]
]

if not datas_invalidas.empty:
    print("\nExemplos de datas inválidas ou ausentes:")
    display(datas_invalidas.head(20))

Parameters
C C: float, default=1.0

Aggressiveness parameter for the passive-aggressive algorithm, see [1].
For PA-I it is the maximum step size. For PA-II it regularizes the
step size (the smaller `C` the more it regularizes).
As a general rule-of-thumb, `C` should be small when the data is noisy. 		1.0
fit_intercept fit_intercept: bool, default=True

Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. If False, the
data is assumed to be already centered. 		True
max_iter max_iter: int, default=1000

The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the
:meth:`~sklearn.linear_model.PassiveAggressiveClassifier.partial_fit` method.

.. versionadded:: 0.19 		1000
tol tol: float or None, default=1e-3

The stopping criterion. If it is not None, the iterations will stop
when (loss > previous_loss - tol).

.. versionadded:: 0.19 		0.001
early_stopping early_stopping: bool, default=False

Whether to use early stopping to terminate training when validation
score is not improving. If set to True, it will automatically set aside
a stratified fraction of training data as validation and terminate
training when validation score is not improving by at least `tol` for
`n_iter_no_change` consecutive epochs.

.. versionadded:: 0.20 		False
validation_fraction validation_fraction: float, default=0.1

The proportion of training data to set aside as validation set for
early stopping. Must be between 0 and 1.
Only used if early_stopping is True.

.. versionadded:: 0.20 		0.1
n_iter_no_change n_iter_no_change: int, default=5

Number of iterations with no improvement to wait before early stopping.

.. versionadded:: 0.20 		5
shuffle shuffle: bool, default=True

Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch. 		True
verbose verbose: int, default=0

The verbosity level. 		0
loss loss: str, default="hinge"

The loss function to be used:
hinge: equivalent to PA-I in the reference paper.
squared_hinge: equivalent to PA-II in the reference paper. 		'hinge'
n_jobs n_jobs: int or None, default=None

The number of CPUs to use to do the OVA (One Versus All, for
multi-class problems) computation.
``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
for more details. 		None
random_state random_state: int, RandomState instance, default=None

Used to shuffle the training data, when ``shuffle`` is set to
``True``. Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple
function calls.
See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`. 		None
warm_start warm_start: bool, default=False

When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as
initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution.
See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.

Repeatedly calling fit or partial_fit when warm_start is True can
result in a different solution than when calling fit a single time
because of the way the data is shuffled. 		False
class_weight class_weight: dict, {class_label: weight} or "balanced" or None, default=None

Preset for the class_weight fit parameter.

Weights associated with classes. If not given, all classes
are supposed to have weight one.

The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.

parameter *class_weight* to automatically weight samples. 		None

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ============================================================
# CONFIGURAÇÃO
# ============================================================
# Os resultados de Nov/Dez de 2019 abaixo foram digitalizados da
# figura de referência enviada pelo usuário, pois a imagem não contém
# os valores numéricos brutos. Eles são usados apenas para reproduzir
# os dois pontos iniciais do mesmo modelo.

MESES = [
    "Nov 2019", "Dec 2019",
    "Jan 2020", "Feb 2020", "Mar 2020", "Apr 2020",
    "May 2020", "Jun 2020", "Jul 2020", "Aug 2020",
    "Sep 2020", "Oct 2020", "Nov 2020", "Dec 2020"
]

# Nov/Dez 2019 - valores obtidos da imagem de referência
BASE_2019 = {
    "Perceptron": [0.4884, 0.3765],
    "SGDClassifier": [0.3778, 0.3329],
    "PassiveAggressiveClassifier": [0.4870, 0.3745],
    "MultinomialNB": [0.4643, 0.5933],
}

# Jan-Dez 2020 - resultados do treinamento_mes()
# Ordem original do retorno da função:
# (MultinomialNB, SGDClassifier, Perceptron, PassiveAggressiveClassifier)
RESULTADOS_2020 = [
    (0.28585829493087556, 0.30952380952380953, 0.30952380952380953, 0.30952380952380953),
    (0.5066957334163812,  0.3246753246753247,  0.5491224389902805,  0.49743589743589745),
    (0.6029329997219905,  0.37658227848101267, 0.70378224158538,    0.6630247470033797),
    (0.756743295019157,   0.4040735873850197,  0.8490310307930091,  0.844234249706065),
    (0.6379675179049411,  0.3895800933125972,  0.8536406252378126,  0.8536333177013),
    (0.6540770507272313,  0.44695378151260506, 0.8717720129135871,  0.8657161803713528),
    (0.6404879079917709,  0.5191234971220304,  0.8669716028206594,  0.8783659842981877),
    (0.6358745094976865,  0.5528587075575028,  0.8704107157266199,  0.8789760940432678),
    (0.6239828591834305,  0.5504712789359439,  0.8802655677655677,  0.888902001510574),
    (0.5834204319289436,  0.5122290713859614,  0.8728738311273898,  0.8876771325368158),
    (0.731759097919045,   0.6306446964419038,  0.8543038486224357,  0.8957406572838793),
    (0.7576244075479717,  0.6811853143043904,  0.898189557239614,   0.9073328752331403),
]

# ============================================================
# MONTA O DATAFRAME E SALVA EM PICKLE
# ============================================================

mnb = [r[0] for r in RESULTADOS_2020]
sgd = [r[1] for r in RESULTADOS_2020]
perceptron = [r[2] for r in RESULTADOS_2020]
pa = [r[3] for r in RESULTADOS_2020]

# DataFrame no mesmo formato visual da figura: 14 pontos por método
# (Nov/19, Dez/19 e Jan-Dez/20)
df_scores = pd.DataFrame({
    "month": MESES,
    "Perceptron": BASE_2019["Perceptron"] + perceptron,
    "SGDClassifier": BASE_2019["SGDClassifier"] + sgd,
    "PassiveAggressiveClassifier": BASE_2019["PassiveAggressiveClassifier"] + pa,
    "MultinomialNB": BASE_2019["MultinomialNB"] + mnb,
})

PICKLE_PATH = str(RESULT_DIR / "dfScores_feedback_2020.pkl")
FIG_PATH = str(RESULT_DIR / "grafico_feedback_2020.png")

df_scores.to_pickle(PICKLE_PATH)

# ============================================================
# CARREGA O PICKLE PARA PLOTAR
# ============================================================

df_plot = pd.read_pickle(PICKLE_PATH)

# ============================================================
# ESTILO DA FIGURA ORIGINAL
# ============================================================

x = np.arange(len(df_plot))

estilos = {
    "Perceptron": {
        "color": "orange",
        "marker": "o",
    },
    "SGDClassifier": {
        "color": "brown",
        "marker": "s",
    },
    "PassiveAggressiveClassifier": {
        "color": "blue",
        "marker": "^",
    },
    "MultinomialNB": {
        "color": "green",
        "marker": "v",
    },
}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 10))

for metodo, estilo in estilos.items():
    y = df_plot[metodo].to_numpy()

    # Nov-Dez/2019: trecho pontilhado como na referência
    ax.plot(
        x[:2], y[:2],
        color=estilo["color"],
        marker=estilo["marker"],
        linestyle=":",
        linewidth=2.0,
        markersize=8,
        label=metodo,
        zorder=3,
    )

    # Dez/2019 -> Jan/2020: transição pontilhada vermelha da figura original
    ax.plot(
        x[1:3], y[1:3],
        color="red",
        linestyle=":",
        linewidth=1.4,
        zorder=2,
    )

    # Jan-Dez/2020: resultados do novo experimento
    ax.plot(
        x[2:], y[2:],
        color=estilo["color"],
        marker=estilo["marker"],
        linestyle="-",
        linewidth=1.6,
        markersize=8,
        zorder=3,
    )

# Área cinza de Nov/Dez 2019
ax.axvspan(0, 1, alpha=0.20, color="gray", zorder=0)

# Eixo Y no mesmo padrão da referência
ax.set_ylim(0.10, 1)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0.10, 1, 0.02))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=14)

# Eixo X
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(df_plot["month"], rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=14)

# Rótulo
ax.set_ylabel("F-measure", fontsize=16)

# Grid horizontal
ax.grid(axis="y", linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.65)

# Anotação visual da referência
ax.annotate(
    "Expectation at the end of 2019",
    xy=(0.65, 0.82),
    xytext=(1.50, 0.85),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor="black", shrink=0.05),
    fontsize=15,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", fc="white", ec="black"),
)

# Chave/brace visual sobre Nov-Dez 2019
ax.annotate(
    "}",
    xy=(0.45, 0.795),
    xytext=(0.45, 0.795),
    fontsize=55,
    rotation=90,
    ha="center",
    va="center",
)

# Legenda no topo, mesma ordem da figura de referência
ax.legend(
    loc="lower left",
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.005, 1.0, 0.102),
    mode="expand",
    borderaxespad=0.0,
    ncol=4,
    fontsize=14,
    frameon=True,
)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG_PATH, format="png", bbox_inches="tight", dpi=500)
plt.show()

print(df_plot)
print(f"\nPickle salvo em: {PICKLE_PATH}")
print(f"Figura salva em: {FIG_PATH}")
